children: Ares Management closed a nearly $4 billion fund focused on Japanese logistics real-estate development as it continues to invest in the country's infrastructure market.

The fund,called Japan Logistics Development Partners V LP, attracted 612 billion yen, equivalent to $3.83 billion, in commitments from pension funds, sovereign-wealth funds and insurance companies, financial institutions and other investors across North America, Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Middle East.
The Los Angeles-based alternative-investment manager's fifth such fund will invest in institutional-quality modern logistics facilities in key Japanese markets, including Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya.
It has already committed to projects representing around Y450 billion in total investment, Ares said.
The Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, a cornerstone investor, committed around Y150 billion in equity, it added.
The fund is larger than its 2021 predecessor and represents Ares's biggest closed-end real-estate fundraising to date. Ares Real Estate managed about $121 billion in assets as of June 30.

"Japan remains one of the most attractive logistics markets globally, supported by long-term structural demand for modern supply-chain infrastructure," said Yoshiyuki Chosa, Ares partner and head of Japan real estate.
